title: LEFT JOIN dropped databases
description: Fix the query so the result contains exactly two columns: database_name and state. Every database must remain in the result; each matching active session should produce a row with state = active, while a database with no active sessions must appear with state = NULL. Sort by database_name ASC.
starter_sql:
SELECT d.name AS database_name, s.state
FROM databases AS d
LEFT JOIN sessions AS s ON s.database_id = d.id
WHERE s.state = 'active'
ORDER BY d.name;
hints: Check whether the right-table condition is in WHERE.
Make the active condition part of ON.
solution_explanation: WHERE on s.state removed NULL-extended rows after LEFT JOIN. Moving it into ON preserves every database.
